narrative.overview:
A sheet of paper on a desk, and beside it one column of ink in a careful hand. The document is the witness; the interface is the marginal note that points at it. Dues looks calm because it only speaks where it knows something: a box where a value was found, a hatched gap where it was not, a second line naming the Payment as the other witness.

The posh comes from restraint. One large serif number, generous space around it, hairlines instead of boxes, one accent used for evidence and the next action. Finished work goes quiet: confirmed is plain ink and a tick, never green. Density is low on the things that matter and tight on the rest: a 56px total over 40px rows.
keyCharacteristics: One hero per screen: the invoice total, set large in serif, with its printed twin cropped from the page directly above it.
State is a glyph plus two or three words. Colour only reinforces.
Hairlines and tints, not cards. One shadow in the whole product, under the paper.
The document is never restyled: light in both themes, never inverted.
Keyboard first on laptop: the primary button's label always says what `Enter` will do.

rules.name: The No Green Rule
rules.body: There is no success colour. Confirmed is `ink` and a tick; finished work recedes.

rules.name: The Value Is Ink Rule
rules.body: State colour belongs to the glyph and the state line. A value is always `ink`, whatever its state.

rules.name: The Red Means Payment Rule
rules.body: `bad` appears only when a value disagrees with the Payment. Never for validation, never for emphasis.

rules.name: The Tint Label Rule
rules.body: On a focused row or a stop (`accent-bg`, `warn-bg`, `bad-bg`, Sheet Shade) labels and muted placeholders ("Nothing read", "Choose 1 or 2") step up from `ink-3` to `ink-2` to hold 4.5:1.

rules.name: The One Big Number Rule
rules.body: Only the total is set in Hero. Nothing else on the screen exceeds Title.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Bill numbers, GSTINs and References use Inter with `"tnum","zero","ss02"` so 0/O and 1/I/l cannot be confused.

rules.name: The Exact Money Rule
rules.body: `Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', {style:'currency', currency:'INR', minimumFractionDigits:2})`. Always two decimals, Indian grouping, never rounded. A difference is written with amount and direction: "≠ Payment ₹1,180.00 · ₹30.00 less".

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only paper and things floating above the whole screen cast a shadow. Rows, cards and buttons never do.

rules.name: The Paper Stays Paper Rule
rules.body: In dark mode the page keeps its own colours at `brightness(.92)` with a hairline edge. It is never inverted.

dos: Do give every state a glyph and two or three plain words: "On the page", "Check this", "Not found on page", "Nothing read", "Differs from Payment", "Confirmed".
Do show absence as an absence: the hatched slot, the camera at fit, no box.
Do keep a disagreement with the Payment visible in glyph and words after the value is confirmed, on the evidence line, on the primary button and in the field's accessible name.
Do keep every tag beside the value it names, and every floating layer off the primary button.
Do make the primary button's label the literal next action with its value.
Do keep the document light in both themes and the box colours fixed.
Do right-align amounts in columns; left-align the hero when it stands alone in the rail.
donts: Don't say "confidence", "AI", "verified" or show a percentage.
Don't draw a box, crop or leader for a value that was not located, or shade a box to mean "less sure".
Don't add green, a second accent, a second shadow, or a filled key hint.
Don't colour a value by its state, or carry any state by colour alone.
Don't set anything but the total in Hero type.
Don't let a tag or label sit on top of printed text the Claimant has to read.
Don't say "differs from the document" where there is no text layer under the field, or box a typed amount on a number that is not an amount.
Don't draw focus twice: one ring, no side bar.
